### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const), HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `409d4682368db65d9a588cb894e719637b80e00b` — the merge of head `0acd17d22771e033de2fe8233b64433119c187ff` into base `c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 409d4682368db65d9a588cb894e719637b80e00b && git checkout 409d4682368db65d9a588cb894e719637b80e00b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe 0acd17d22771e033de2fe8233b64433119c187ff && git checkout -B drift-repro c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe && git merge --no-ff 0acd17d22771e033de2fe8233b64433119c187ff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- 用户能看到什么变化：写钩子或脚本动作的作者，如果用 `ctx.text?.('键')` 或 `ctx.text!('键')` 这两种写法去取一句没有声明的文案，现在保存时就会被拒，提示与普通写法 `ctx.text('键')` 相同；以前要等到运行时才报错。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `269566b8c479ac1c9192593eee89ef8904a88bdd` · 2026-11-19T23:44Z

- **Shape** — draft, base `main`, 7 files, +120/−11. Merge-base `c0716ed4`. The branch carries #35636's history, which was squashed on main. The three-dot diff and GitHub's file list are the same 7 files, and the last main merge `7a158d4b` shows 0 `@@@` hunks. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35686`: NOT governed, 0 of 7 paths.
  - `Fixes #35512`.
  - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. That is the canonical breaking spelling, and the claim's `yes (narrowing)` (the widening-plus-narrowing arm) was wrong for a diff that only narrows. The deviation is accepted.
  - The `Skills-docs: none` reason holds. Both skills teach the rule without naming a call shape, so they become true for more shapes and say nothing false.
  - `@objectstack/spec` minor, with FROM/TO.
- **The reader** — `TEXT_CALL` gains `(?:\s*\?\.|[ \t]*!)?` between `text` and `\s*\(`. I traced the edges:
  - `ctx.text?.('k')` matches, and so does `ctx.text ?. ('k')`. A `?.` on the next line is still an optional call in JS and is read, which is correct.
  - `ctx.text!('k')` and `ctx.text !('k')` match.
  - `ctx.text\n!('k')` does not match, because the `!` takes only blanks, so ASI ends the statement. Pinned.
  - `ctx.text !== x` does not match: `\s*\(` fails.
  - The leading `(?<![\w$.])` and the key and quote groups are unchanged. Comments and long strings are still blanked first.
  - It stays one reader behind both doors (`hookTextKeysAskedIn`, used by `HookSchema` and `ActionSchema`), so the hook and the action cannot drift.
  - `ctx?.text(` and `ctx!.text(` are left out, as the acceptance notes declare. They stay judged at run time, which is the safe side.
- **Why the narrowing is safe** — the key it now refuses is one the runtime already refused on every run, with a fault naming the hook or action and the key. A declared key passes in every shape (CONTROL, per shape), and so does a computed key.
  - Observation, not blocking: a `js` body cannot hold `!` (it is TypeScript-only syntax), so that arm can only bite TypeScript source. It is harmless either way, because it refuses only a key the run would refuse.
- **ADR-0087** — the new entry `hook-action-text-key-optional-call-refused` has a surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria. There is no tombstone and no D2 conversion, because which sentence was meant is a judgement. It is registered through the changeset marker.
- **Pins**
  - `hook-texts.test.ts` and `action-texts.test.ts` each cover the four shapes (plain or `await`, `?.` or `!`). Each refusal carries the existing sentence (`undeclaredHookTextKeyAtSave` / `undeclaredActionTextKeyAtSave`) at `body.source`, and each shape has a declared-plus-computed CONTROL. The hook file also has the whitespace and next-line-`!` case.
  - The pins went red first (12 failed), and the ablation turns 13 red. The dogfood battery is green at this head (dev report 7024765229).
  - Not re-measured here: no `node_modules`.
- **Docs** — `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx:500` 「names it literally in `ctx.text('key')`」 is incomplete but not wrong. My call: nothing owed. It can ride a later docs touch.
- **Gates** — on this head: 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure. Mergeable `clean`.
- **Landing terms** — not governed, but **L2 owed** (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) for the narrowing and the new ADR-0087 entry. It is running in an isolated reviewer. The seat or card thread lands this head after a `## Contract review` **PASS** on it, with all checks green. A new push needs a fresh L1 unless it is a clean main merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `269566b8c479ac1c9192593eee89ef8904a88bdd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.hook-action-text-key-optional-call-refused.ts + packages/spec/src/data/hook-texts.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-texts.test.ts
Security-touching: no

### ① Derived judgments

Read for this record: card #35512 (body and all 5 comments), PR #35686 (body, its 2 comments, the 7 files, the net diff from merge base `c0716ed4`) and the 69 check-runs on the head. The head did not move during the review.

1. **`HookSchema` accept set narrows: right.** A hook that declares `texts` and whose code asks `ctx.text?.('k')` for a key `texts` does not declare is now refused, at `body.source` for a `js` body and at `handler` for an inline function (the door reads the function's own compiled source, `hook.zod.ts:276-292`). Hook `texts` shipped in 18.6.0 (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:504`), so this narrows a published accept set. It is the refusal the `HookSchema.texts` TSDoc already stated and the runtime already made when the call ran.
2. **`ActionSchema` accept set narrows the same way at `body.source`: right, and no break against any release.** `ActionSchema.texts` is itself unreleased (`.changeset/34374-action-texts-org-locale.md` is still pending), so the action half ships already narrowed.
3. **`ctx.text!('k')` with an undeclared key in a `js` body is now refused on both doors: right as a refusal, wrong as described.** No document that could run is lost. The description is S1 in ④.
4. **Nothing widens.** `TEXT_CALL` feeds only `hookTextKeysAskedIn`, and its two callers (`hook.zod.ts:362`, `action.zod.ts:2683`) turn each undeclared key into an issue, so reading more shapes can only add refusals. Nothing refused on `main` is accepted here.
5. **Public surface: unchanged.** No export, type, key, enum member or error code is added or removed. `hookTextKeysAskedIn` keeps its signature and returns more keys for the same source; the two doors are its only callers in the tree.
6. **Sentences and JSON Schema: unchanged.** The two save-refusal sentences keep their bytes, and no `.describe()` string moves.
7. **The step-18 ledger gains one entry.** It records the narrowing; it is not an accept set.

### ② Semver level

- **Level.** `@objectstack/spec: minor` matches. A `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3), and spec is the only package moved. No check-run on the head is red, `Check Changeset` included.
- **Kind.** `narrowed` matches: a document an author could save is refused. The hook half alone carries it (judgment 1).
- **Clause ② line.** `no (narrowing)`, as the PR body and the changeset declare, is what the repo's definition requires. The value answers one question: does the diff widen an accept set or enlarge the public surface (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:90`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md:72`). This diff does neither (judgments 4 and 5). The same file reserves `yes (narrowing)` for "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another" (`:113`) and defines `no (narrowing)` as "NOT a widening, but breaking" (`:115`), and `execution-duties.md:110` says a card that narrows a published accept set is `no`. So the claim's `yes (narrowing)` (comment 7023306761, and the released claim 7022933757 before it) declared a widening the card never had. `os-dev.md:276` tells the dev to copy the claim's two lines unchanged; the dev departed from it and said so in the report, and the departure is correct. The seat should correct the claim line on the card so the card and the PR agree. That is a card edit and does not move the head.
- **ADR-0087.** Matches what a declared narrowing owes. The changeset carries one marker, `registered hook-action-text-key-optional-call-refused`. The id is new in this diff, and its file name is the id under step 18, the current protocol major. `no-migration-prescription` is closed to a `narrowed` changeset, so a new entry is the route. No tombstone is owed (no key leaves) and no D2 conversion (which key the author meant is a judgement).
- **BREAKING section.** The banner, FROM, TO and the one-line fix are all present, and both declaration lines sit at line start in the changeset body. Its content is right for `?.(` and wrong for `!(` (S1). Its action clause describes a break no released version can meet (N1).
- **Title.** It carries no `!`. Nothing requires one: the banner, the arm and the kind each carry the breaking signal.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is empty in the report. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, the clause line: answered in ②.
- Deviation, a title without `!`: accepted (②).
- Deviation, the branch recreated by a plain push after #35636 merged: no effect on the contract. The net diff from the merge base is exactly the 7 files.
- Out of scope, `ctx?.text(` and `ctx!.text(` stay run-time refusals: accepted. The TSDoc names the spellings the save reads and sends every other key to run time, so the text is exact about them. No card is owed until a producer is measured.
- The PR body's skills-and-docs line says `none`. Its reason holds for the two skill files it names: `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md:875` and `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md:151` name no call shape. It is silent on `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx:499-501`, which does name one: a key is refused at save "if the hook names it literally in `ctx.text('key')`, otherwise when the hook runs". After this diff that sentence is incomplete, not wrong. Its instruction (declare the key) and its example still hold, but "otherwise when the hook runs" now misplaces `ctx.text?.('key')`, which is refused at save. It errs toward promising less than the door does. One sentence there should name the optional call, or name no spelling, as the skills do. It should not teach `ctx.text!(` for a `js` body (S1). That is a prose edit or a follow-up card, and the line should then read `follow-up owed` with that file. `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx:228-231` names no shape and holds.
- Dogfood. On a pull request neither dogfood leg runs: both check-runs are skipped and the `Dogfood Regression Gate` roll-up counts zero legs (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2751`). The battery this narrowing owes has one witness on this head, the dev's local run in the report (482 files, 4092 tests, none red). The queue build runs the shards before landing.
- Check-runs on the head: 58 success, 11 skipped, none red.
- `main` is at `03865ae9`, 12 commits past the merge base. None touches a file of this diff.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no data access.
- Author: the PR was opened by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, the relay. There is no other login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — the `ctx.text!(` shape is taught as a legal call in a `js` body, and its FROM describes something that never happened.

- **What the save can see.** A hook's save reads a `js` body's `source`, else an inline handler's `Function.prototype.toString()` (`hook.zod.ts:276-292`). An action's save reads `body.source` alone (`action.zod.ts:2666-2686`). A non-null `!` is TypeScript and has no JavaScript form. Whatever turns a handler into a function (esbuild under the CLI loader and vitest, `tsc`, native type stripping) erases it first, so a handler's `ctx.text!('k')` reaches the door as the plain call, which `main` already refuses. In a `js` body, `ctx.text!('k')` on one line is a syntax error. The sandbox evaluates the source as written, inside an async arrow function (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts:432`), so the body throws before its first statement, whatever `texts` declares.
- **What follows.** The `!` arm of `TEXT_CALL` matches one input only: TypeScript pasted into a `js` body. Refusing that earlier is harmless. Four sentences around it are not accurate:
  - Entry `replacement`, line 18: "ctx.text?.(KEY) and ctx.text!(KEY) stay legal for a declared key." On `body.source`, the first surface the entry names, `ctx.text!(KEY)` does not compile. An action that carries it is refused at the authoring doors as `action-body-does-not-compile` (the step-18 entry `action-body-does-not-compile-refused`). A hook that carries it saves clean, because the hook parse check reads the body as TypeScript and only warns (`packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.ts:670`), and then throws on every run.
  - Entry `reason`, lines 22-23, and the changeset FROM: "the runtime refused the key only when the code ran, as a fault naming the hook or action and the key." That is true for `?.(`. For `!(` the runtime never reached the key.
  - The changeset's fix line: "A declared key is accepted in every shape."
  - The `ActionSchema.texts` TSDoc (`action.zod.ts:1575-1577`) lists `ctx.text!('key')` among the ways the body asks, on a schema whose only code is a `js` body.
- **Why it matters.** The entry is the prescription `os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide print, and the TSDoc is what an author, often an AI, reads before writing a body. A hook body written to those sentences passes save and throws on every run.
- **Fix, one of two.** Keep the arm and say where a `!` can occur: it is TypeScript, a handler's is erased before the save reads it, and one in `body.source` must be removed, not kept. That touches the entry's four fields, the changeset and the TSDoc sites. Or drop the `!` arm and its mentions and keep `?.(` alone. Either way, add one pin on the `handler` path: an inline handler asking `ctx.text?.('undeclared')`, refused at `handler`. That is the strict-TypeScript scenario the card is accepted against, and the new pins drive `body.source` only.

Each file, beyond S1:

- `hook-refusal-codes.ts`: the `?.` arm holds. It reads a legal JavaScript optional call, with whitespace or a line break on either side, on both inputs the doors read, behind the same mask for comments and longer strings. The `!` arm is held to one line, which matches JavaScript (a `!` on the next line starts a new statement) and TypeScript alike. The pattern has no nested quantifier and adds no backtracking cost. It introduces no false reading of its own; the one it inherits is N2.
- `hook.zod.ts`: both TSDoc hunks agree with the reader. The `HookSchema.texts` sentence is true for all three spellings as an author writes them, the `!` one through erasure in a handler. No `.describe()` string is touched.
- `action.zod.ts`: TSDoc only. See S1.
- The entry: all four required fields are present, the file name is derived from the id, and it carries no `relevantWhen`, so it is always listed, which is the safe default. Its content: S1 and N1.
- The two test files: each shape has a lit pin and a dark pin on `body.source` for both doors, and the hook file adds the whitespace and next-line controls. They agree with the reader. The `!(` pins hand a `js` body a line that is not JavaScript, which is the S1 case.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the BREAKING banner and the entry's `surface` name the action half as a break. `ActionSchema.texts` is unreleased, so no released document is refused there. Harmless; reword with S1 or leave.
- N2 (nit) — inherited, in the unchanged tail of `TEXT_CALL`: the reader stops at the closing quote, so `ctx.text?.('follow_up' + x)` reads `follow_up` as a literal key. `main` does the same for the plain call, and this diff carries it to two more shapes. A follow-up card, not a fix here.
- N3 (nit) — two internal docblocks still name the plain call alone: `refuseUndeclaredLiteralTextKey` (`hook.zod.ts:338-339`) and `refuseUndeclaredLiteralActionTextKey` (`action.zod.ts:2661-2662`).
- N4 (nit) — accepted as they are: the refusal sentence echoes `ctx.text('k')` whichever spelling the author wrote (the key is the anchor and the bytes are pinned), and the entry spells calls with their opening parenthesis against the entries README's advice (no live ratchet matches, and here the call shape is the surface).

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
